annotations.text:
RACK FIRST — one direction, done properly.

The rack, its faceplates, real ports from the engine's catalogue, and cables that sag between them are the product. Everything else hangs off that.

What I took from Homelable: the slack-loop cable (bows right and down, more on longer runs), real RJ45/SFP jack shapes at a fixed size, patch-facing gear always shows ports and everything else reveals on hover, one cable per port, copper-or-fibre decided by the port you start from.

What I took from elsewhere: Patchdocs lights the WHOLE physical path on one hover — that is the answer to your crossing complaint. Device42 keeps power and data cabling on separate toggles. Meraki/Mist put L2/L3 facts on the port, so you never leave the rack to read them.

What I dropped: the building view (not necessary — you said so), the black triangle cursors (presence is now a dashed ring on the device someone is editing plus a name chip on the rail; a held port gets a dashed ring too), and the six-tab bar.
Kept for the record. You rejected all eight on 2026-09-11 — the rack was not the centrepiece in any of them, and the building view hid crossings. Nothing here is in play.

Answered 2026-09-11:
✓ COLOUR IS THE REAL SHEATH. The hue on screen is the lead in your hand, so a cable you are holding can be found here and the reverse. Type is carried by the LINE, not the colour — copper one stroke, fibre a pair, power heavy. Grey, blue, red, yellow, green, orange, purple, black, white are stock lead colours, set per cable.
✓ Four port glyphs: RJ45, SFP+ (bail), LC (two ferrules), C14 (power).
✓ PSUs, PDU, and power on its own rail lane.
✓ Rear view: stacked under the front when zoomed.

ONE COLLISION, WORTH KNOWING: red, green and orange are also the reserved risk colours. The rule that keeps them apart is LOCATION — the canvas shows sheath colours only, and risk never appears as colour on the canvas, only in panels and badges. If that feels too subtle, the alternative is a restricted lead palette that avoids those three hues. Your call.

Still open:
• Portal trays, or a cable that visibly runs off the edge?
• Presence with no cursors — enough?

GOING INSIDE A BOX

Same gesture as going inside a rack. The physical ports on the left edge are the far side of the ports you cabled in the rack, so a trace crosses the boundary without changing view.

A guest is a node in the same graph as a switch, and its vNIC is a port. That is why a trace can start on a VM and end at the internet.

The firewall board is the teaching one: four bands left to right — where traffic enters, what it is called, what decides, where it leaves. It shows the policies in the order the device reads them and marks the two that can never be reached. It never says permitted or denied.

The config board carries the assistant. Its six rules are printed ON the screen, not in a help page: it reads this config and this graph only, cites a line for every claim, cannot see credentials because they were destroyed at the gate, never says permitted or denied, says 'I could not establish this' rather than guessing, and never changes the estate.
